pairs.subject: simulated-audience-testing
pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-sim/src/decision.rs:78 The coverage gate leaves not_provoked checks out of its denominator, so a cell whose hard-rule checks were mostly never provoked still counts as covered and can win; separately, the calibration schema cannot source population mixes and the near-miss flag never reaches the report.

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-sim/src/decision.rs:78 The new decision.rs fixes most of the earlier verdict: hard fails are counted per run, quality ties use per-run SE, and ties go to cost per usable stream (latency only after that). The coverage share still excludes not_provoked, which the technique's coverage gate names as unmeasured. Latency ceilings are tiebreakers rather than declared gates. Over-refusal is not reported beside quality.

crates/shadowrunr-sim/src/calibration.rs:81 Archetypes, sizes and tactics carry source_ids, and assumptions() reports them. Population mixes are bare f64 maps with no source field, and assumptions() never lists them, so the archetype proportions are unauditable.

crates/shadowrunr-sim/src/judge.rs:173 Situations become situation:<id> hard rules, with injection ledger and attempts recorded. But catalog::Situation.near_miss is never read anywhere in the sim crate (grep found 0 hits), so over-refusal is never reported as a separate axis from violation.

crates/shadowrunr-sim/src/judge.rs:404 A same-tier judge is refused. The judge never sees the constitution (judge.rs:1), the transcript is fenced with a per-run nonce, the system prompt is byte-identical across runs, and quotes are verified, with unverified claims marked not_evaluable. Gap: no human-agreement calibration of the judge exists (grep found none).

crates/shadowrunr-sim/src/outcome.rs:13 Run states are judged, judge_void, judge_pending and engine_failed, classified from the ledger with CUT_TAIL/CUT_SHARE thresholds. Rule states include not_provoked and not_evaluable. Pending and engine-failed runs are excluded from every count (summary.rs Excluded).

crates/shadowrunr-sim/src/instrument.rs:296 The judge tier now joins the per-run hash. The hash also covers LF-normalised per-file digests, a base/axis split, optional components that join only when present, and a SIM_LOGIC_VERSION fallback. Cells are keyed by instrument_hash, so results are never pooled.

pairs.subject: simulated-audience-testing
pairs.evidence: sim/calibration.json:530 Every named population mix (small_new_channel, growing_channel, raid_moment, hostile_raid) gives archetype proportions as bare numbers with no source or ASSUMPTION label, so the audience mix each room size uses cannot be audited.

techniques.evidence: sim/calibration.json:530 Sources, audience_sizes and archetypes cite source_ids, and the assumption source points to its derivation. The populations block (lines 528-568) has no source per number. Some entries also mix real sources with 'assumption' without saying which part was assumed (e.g. audience size 3).

sim/rubric.toml:14 The rubric is written for a blind reader (line 3), and matrices route a different tier as judge. But it adds 0-3 scaled rows, while the standard holds that rubric rows are checkable facts, never scales. pacing_no_dead_air also asks the judge to check a 20 s silence that code could count.
sim/rubric.toml:5 The rubric and calibration are both hashed (instrument.rs:245-249). night-opus.toml is a separate design judged by Sonnet.
sim/rubric.toml:10 Hard rules declare all four rule states.

sim/rubric.toml:21 Each rubric row declares a provocation kind (always/situation/closed_vote/pinned_link). The near-miss bank lives in characters/, and its unreported over-refusal axis is judged on sim-runner-judging.
sim/rubric.toml:13 Hard rules are held at a 100% bar (line 9), and quality is declared non-gating before any run.

pairs.registryProposal: cheapest-passing-tier-selection could state explicitly whether not_provoked checks belong in the coverage denominator; an implementation read 'evaluated share' as pass+fail over pass+fail+not_evaluable. The golden path's 'Neither kind is a scale' rule appears in no technique's decision rules, so a rubric adding non-gating 0-3 scales passes every technique read alone.
